caption: A pigeon walks past outside a window fitted with coloured glass panes and appears red, then blue, then yellow as it passes behind each pane.

sa.check: A pigeon walks past outside a window fitted with coloured glass panes.
It appears red, blue and yellow as it passes behind each pane.
The order of colours is red, then blue, then yellow.

pc.expect: The pigeon takes the colour of whichever pane it is behind and looks grey through the clear gaps.
pc.fail: It is grey behind a coloured pane; or coloured through a clear gap; or a colour the panes do not have.

pc.expect: The colour changes exactly at each pane's edge.
pc.fail: It changes mid-pane; or lags behind the edge; or changes with the bird still.

pc.expect: The panes themselves do not change colour and the bird keeps its shape.
pc.fail: A pane changes colour; or the bird changes shape; or the panes rearrange.

pc.expect: The bird walks steadily and the window stays still.
pc.fail: The bird jumps position; or the window moves; or the colours shift with the bird still.
A second bird appears; or a pane vanishes; or the bird passes through the glass.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The window frame and the ground stay the same.
pc.fail: The frame changes; or the ground changes; or the bird's true colour changes when seen through clear glass.

note: The pigeon is self-driven; only the tint through the panes is judged.
